title: Sable and the Portrait
premise: Edmund Oyelaran, a nonbinary teacher haunted by a decade of unexplained noises in their rented cottage, takes a post at Marrowfen School, where students have been vanishing from class lists for fifty years. When Edmund's sleep-recording app captures a second voice answering questions Edmund never asked aloud, they discover the school's 1974 art prize portrait was stolen from a dead student named Sable, whose spirit has been trading memories for time ever since. To end the disappearances, Edmund must return the portrait to Sable's unmarked grave before the winter solstice, when the school's founding bargain comes due and claims a living student in her place. Edmund succeeds at terrible cost — surrendering their own dearest memory of belonging — and the final chapter reveals Sable finally at rest while Edmund learns to build new memories worth keeping.
about_author: Bram Vasquez is the pen name of a former night-shift school caretaker who spent years listening to empty hallways and writing down what they heard. They live near a decommissioned boarding school and insist, politely, that the portraits there are all accounted for.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk Problem
chapters.summary: Edmund arrives at Marrowfen School for the autumn term and notices the register lists more students than seats. A colleague, Mrs. Adeyemi, warns them not to ask about the class of '74. POV: Edmund. Beat: unease dressed as professional curiosity; the reader feels the school watching back.

chapters.title: Noises With Explanations
chapters.summary: In the cottage behind the school, Edmund catalogs ten years of rational explanations: pipes, settling beams, wind. But tonight the scratching spells something against the wall. POV: Edmund. Beat: the comfort of denial beginning to crack; dread arrives as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Edmund plays back their sleep app out of boredom and hears a second voice — dry, patient, young — answering questions Edmund never asked: 'Yes. No. She took it.' POV: Edmund with intercut transcript fragments. Beat: vertigo; the private space of sleep is no longer private.

chapters.title: Sable
chapters.summary: Digging through the archive, Edmund finds a 1974 yearbook: Sable Iwu, art prize winner, photo removed, name inked over. The librarian denies she existed. POV: Edmund. Beat: the thrill of proof curdling into isolation — everyone here has agreed to forget.

chapters.title: What the Students Know
chapters.summary: A quiet pupil, Tova, draws the missing classroom from memory: same desks, same window, a girl painting at an easel. She says the vanishing kids 'go where it's warm.' POV: alternating Edmund and Tova. Beat: tenderness and terror braided; a child's calm is worse than panic.

chapters.title: The Portrait's Frame
chapters.summary: Behind the headmaster's office paneling, Edmund finds an empty frame sized for a portrait, its backing paper inscribed: RETURNED IN FULL OR IN INTEREST. POV: Edmund. Beat: the story pivots from haunting to debt; horror becomes arithmetic.

chapters.title: Second Voice, First Conversation
chapters.summary: Edmund speaks aloud to the recording that night and the voice answers in real time. It is Sable, or what remains, and she asks one question: 'Do you remember being wanted anywhere?' POV: Edmund. Beat: grief replaces fear; the ghost is lonelier than the living.

chapters.title: The Founders' Bargain
chapters.summary: In the parish records, Edmund uncovers the 1924 deed: the school's prosperity was sworn against 'one likeness kept, one child owed, each generation.' POV: Edmund with archival documents. Beat: scale widens — this is institutional sin, not a single ghost.

chapters.title: Mrs. Adeyemi Confesses
chapters.summary: Adeyemi admits she was Sable's classmate and helped hide the theft; the headmaster's family has renewed the bargain every solstice since. POV: Adeyemi. Beat: guilt as inheritance; even the complicit are trapped, and Edmund pities her anyway.

chapters.title: Where It's Warm
chapters.summary: Following Tova's map, Edmund finds the sealed 1974 classroom intact behind the boiler room, easel still standing, air impossibly summer-warm. Something breathes in it. POV: Edmund. Beat: awe tipping into violation; a preserved moment that resents intruders.

chapters.title: The Interest Comes Due
chapters.summary: A student, Pell, doesn't come to afternoon class. His desk is warm. The register crosses his name out by itself. POV: Edmund and, briefly, Pell's disoriented last ordinary hour. Beat: stakes turn mortal; guilt lands on Edmund for asking questions.

chapters.title: Hunting the Portrait
chapters.summary: Edmund traces the painting's path through three decades of estate sales and finds it listed, sold last month, to a buyer in the next county. POV: Edmund on the road. Beat: desperate momentum; hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: The Collector
chapters.summary: The buyer, an elderly man, refuses to sell — he says the girl in the painting watches him sleep, and he likes the company. POV: Edmund negotiating in a house full of wrong things. Beat: moral discomfort; Edmund must take, not ask, and hates it.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Edmund steals the portrait during a power cut and drives through a storm that seems to follow the car. In the rearview mirror, the painted Sable is looking elsewhere now — at them. POV: Edmund. Beat: transgression complete; no clean hands, only necessary ones.

chapters.title: She Took It
chapters.summary: Sable's voice explains at last: the headmaster's daughter stole the portrait in 1974 to win the prize herself, and Sable died chasing it. The bargain bound her theft to the school instead. POV: Sable's monologue over Edmund's driving. Beat: righteous fury; the true villain was human all along.

chapters.title: The Grave Without a Name
chapters.summary: Edmund locates Sable's unmarked plot behind the chapel wall, but the ground refuses the spade, and the warm classroom's presence gathers at the treeline, watching. POV: Edmund. Beat: the world itself resisting correction; loneliness at its most physical.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Pell is found — half-here, fading — and the headmaster offers Edmund a deal: return the portrait to the school vault and keep everything, including Pell, forever borrowed. POV: Edmund weighing it. Beat: temptation crystallized; duty versus love made literal.

chapters.title: What Edmund Would Keep
chapters.summary: To open the grave, Sable needs a memory freely given — one of belonging. Edmund chooses their last good memory of home, and feels it leave like heat leaving a hand. POV: Edmund. Beat: sacrifice without melodrama; love proven by loss.

chapters.title: Returned in Full
chapters.summary: At midnight on the solstice, Edmund lays the portrait on the grave and speaks Sable's full name aloud. The warm classroom exhales; every vanished student steps out of it, older by nothing, blinking at the cold. POV: Edmund and Tova. Beat: climax as release rather than battle; naming as the weapon.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Interest
chapters.summary: The bargain, unpaid, turns on the school: the founders' wing folds inward like paper, taking the headmaster's office and its ledger with it. Adeyemi survives to testify. POV: Adeyemi and Edmund watching from the yard. Beat: justice as collapse; institutions cannot survive their debts.

chapters.title: Register Restored
chapters.summary: Spring term: the register matches the seats. Pell returns changed but whole. Edmund hangs a new painting in the hall — not Sable's likeness, but the classroom window she loved, painted from Tova's description. POV: Edmund. Beat: quiet repair; memory rebuilt deliberately instead of mourned.

chapters.title: One Voice Now
chapters.summary: Edmund plays the sleep app one last time: only their own breathing, then silence, then — faintly, kindly — nothing at all. They keep the recording anyway. POV: Edmund. Beat: resolution as chosen remembrance; belonging is something you make, not something you recover.
